The petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ for the death of Subramanya.
C.V. S/o. Varadappa in a Road Traffic Accident took place on 28.09.2021.
SCCH10 2.

The brief contents of petition are that:
On 28.09.2021 at about 3.10 p.m., the deceased was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA 02KG6184 from Pattegarapalya towards Magadi Road on extreme left side of 4 th Main Road and when he reached at 1st Cross, near S.M.
Industry, Kaveripura, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA02AH4464 was proceeding ahead of deceased motor cycle, with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied brakes in the middle of the road and opened the right side door of said Tata ACE vehicle.
Consequent to which, deceased fell down along with the motor cycle and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, deceased was shifted to Madhu hospital, but inspite of better treatment to save his life, he died on the next day i.e. 29.09.2021 at about 4.15 p.m.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards conveyance, food and nourishment charges, funeral and other incidental charges.
SCCH10 3.

Further the petitioners submitted that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
Jayalakshmi.R vs Santhosh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157193067/
2 aged about 47 years.
He was running business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/p.m.

Further it is the contention of the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the minor daughter and son of the deceased and they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased and due to unexpected death of deceased, they have undergone mental agony and shock and lost bread earning member of the family.
4. Further the petitioners submitted that the Koratagere Police have registered the case against the driver of Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02AH 4464 in Crime No. 122/2021 for the offence punishable u/s 279 and 304A of IPC and Section 134 (A&B) and 187 of MV Act.
The respondent No.1 being RC owner and respondent No.2 being insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they prayed to SCCH10 grant for compensation with interest and cost.

5. In pursuance of the Court notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court,
remained absent and placed exparte, however the respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement in answer to the case of the petitioners.

6. The brief contents of objection statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further this respondent has contended that this respondent is not the insurer of Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg.KA02AH4464 as on the date and time of accident i.e. on 28.09.2021 at 3.10 p.m. and it has issued policy in respect of the offending vehicle in favour of Santosh.
S and the same was valid from 29.09.2021 at 14.48 hrs to 28.09.2022 at 23.59 hrs., as such the policy was not in force as on the date of accident.

Further SCCH10 contended that neither owner nor jurisdictional police complied the mandatory provisions as required under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act in furnishing better particulars within stipulated period of 15 days from the date of alleged accident.
Further contended that the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet u/s 146, 196 of MV Act stating that the offending Tata ACE vehicle was not having any valid insurance at the time of accident.
Further contended that, at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license.
7. Further the respondent No.2 denied the occurrence and mode of accident and also involvement of the offending vehicle.

Further contended that the deceased/rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA02 KG6184 was not having the driving licence to drive the vehicle and he took risk of riding the said motor cycle and it is clear case of volunt9 not fit injuria, as such the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation.
It is SCCH10 contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and without any basis.
Contending the above facts, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition as against it.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :

3 ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 28.09.2021 at about 3.10 p.m., when the deceased by name Subramanya.

No.KA02AH 4464 going ahead of deceased said scooter in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied brakes in the middle of the road and opened the door of said Tata ACE, as a result the deceased fell down and sustained injury and died on the next day at 4.15 p.m., while taking treatment ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the only legal heirs and the dependents of the deceased?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? if so, at what rate and from whom?
 SCCH10  4) What order or award?
9. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 12.

To disprove the case of the petitioners and to prove its defence, the respondent No.2 examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
10.
Heard the arguments from the petitioners.
The learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 have placed the decisions.
Perused the materials available on record 11.

My finding to the aforesaid issues as follows:
 Issue No.1:

The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/
with SCCH10 respect to the death of Subramanya.
C. V in the road traffic accident.

To prove the Jayalakshmi.R vs Santhosh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157193067/
4 accident and the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tata ACE vehicle bearing No. KA 02AH4464, the petitioner No.1, herself got examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12

. Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the PM report, Ex.P.7 is the Inquest report, Ex.P.8 is the Charge sheet and Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12 are the Aadhaar cards.

13. After the accident, Smt. Jayalakshmi who is wife of deceased i.e. petitioner No.1 lodged the complaint against the driver of the Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA02AH4464 and FIR was registered against the driver offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 & 304A of IPC R/w. Sec.134 (A&B), 187 of MV Act.
The FIR and complaint are produced as per Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

Subsequently, after investigation the SCCH10 police have filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 against the driver of the offending Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA02AH4464 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 304A of IPC and Section 134(A&B),187, 146 and 196 of MV Act as the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and ran away from the spot without taking care of the injured and intimation about the alleged accident to the concerned police and the offending vehicle was not having insurance policy as on the date of accident.

The petitioners have also produced the Mahazar, Sketch, vehicles seizures, IMV report, PM report and inquest report as per Ex.P.3 to Ex.P.7.
14.

On other hand, to rebut the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.2 by filing written statement contending that this respondent is not the insurer of Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg.KA 02AH4464 as on the date and time of accident i.e. on 28.09.2021 at 3.10 p.m. and it has issued policy in respect of the SCCH10 offending vehicle in favour of Santosh.
S and the same was valid from 29.09.2021 at 14.48 hrs to 28.09.2022 at 23.59 hrs., as such the policy was not in force as on the date of accident.
The jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet u/s 146, 196 of MV Act stating that the offending Tata ACE vehicle was not having any valid insurance at the time of accident.
Further the respondent No.2 denied the occurrence and mode of accident and also involvement of the offending vehicle.
15. To support of their defence, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and got marked document as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
Ex.R.1 is the copy of Policy, Ex.R.2 is the MLC extract, Ex.R.3 is the Endorsement issued by Government of India and Ex.R.4 is the copy of Application under RTI.
16. The petitioners have produced the FIR and Complaint.

On perusal of the FIR and Complaint it disclose that the FIR was lodged against the driver of the insured vehicle based on complaint as per Ex.P.2.
SCCH10
The petitioners have produced charge sheet as per Ex.P.8.
On perusal of Ex.P.8, it discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of of the offending vehicle.
There is a charge sheet against the owner.
The owner of the vehicle has not at all appeared and disputed the case of the petitioners.

Therefore, by considering oral and documentary evidence, I am of the opinion that,
the accident was occurred due to sole negligen ce of the driver of the offending Tata ACE vehicle Jayalakshmi.R vs Santhosh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157193067/
5 bearing Reg. No.KA02 AH4464.
The petitioners have produced the PM report as per Ex.P.6 and the Inquest report as per Ex.P7, those documents disclose, the deceased died due to consequent upon head injury sustained.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.:2
The petitioners contended that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and the petitioner No.3 is the minor son of the deceased Subramanya.
C. V and they are legal heirs and dependents on the deceased.

To prove the said SCCH10 fact, the petitioners have produced, Aadhaar cards as per Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12 and these documents disclose that the petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife, minor daughter and son of the deceased.
The respondents have not at all disputed the legal heirs of the deceased, except dependency.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased.
Therefore, I answer to the issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ on the death of deceased Subramanya. C. V in the road traffic accident.

The petitioners contended that,
deceased was doing business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/p.m.

In support of the same, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/
p.m. by doing business.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

19. At this juncture, I would like to refer the SCCH10 decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, " C. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 168 - Personal injuries - Determination of compensation - Claimant pleading that he was earning Rs.40,000/ from his transport business - But not producing any material to substantiate his claim Tribunal therefore taking income at Rs.6,000/  In terms of charge prepared by Legal Services Authority income taken at Rs.7,000/ per month - Disability taken as 40% and multiplier of 15 adopted by Tribunal maintained - Total compensation enhanced from Rs.8,46,200/ to Rs.9,23,200/."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.

Therefore in view of the above decision and in the absence of proof of income the income has to be taken into consideration as per the Charge prepared by the SCCH10 Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: The accident was occurred on 28092021.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/ has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
20. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.9, wherein, the birth year of the deceased is shown as 1975.
The accident had taken place on 28.09.2021 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 46 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '13'.
21.

The petitioners have argued that the future prospect has to be taken in to consideration, as per decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
Vs Pranay Sethi and others, if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the Jayalakshmi.R vs Santhosh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157193067/
6
future prospect has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

SCCH10 The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 40 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased Subramanya. C. V was aged about 46 years and as such, 25% is to be added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.18,750/p.m. (Rs.15,000 + Rs.3,750/ i.e. 25%).
22. The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid downs by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.12,500/ p.m. (Rs.18,750 - Rs.6.250 = Rs.12,500/).
23.
The income of the deceased is taken as SCCH10 Rs.12,500/ p.m. and the multiplier 13 is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.19,50,000/ (Rs.12,500/ X 12 X 13).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.19,50,000/ under the head of loss of dependency.

24. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others, the compensation in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

Hence, I award Rs.16,500/ towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/ towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.40,000/ towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
25.

By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion is that, the petitioners are entitled for total SCCH10 compensation of Rs.20,23,000/
under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1) Towards loss of dependency Rs. 19,50,000/
2) Towards loss of Consortium Rs. 40,000/ to the petitioner No.1 3) Towards loss to estate Rs. 16,500/
4) Towards transportation of Rs. 16,500/ dead body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses Total Rs. 20,23,000/
26.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of objection statement, it reveals that, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and the insurer of Tata ACE bearing Reg.No.KA02 AH4464 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

Jayalakshmi.R vs Santhosh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157193067/
7 27.

In this case, the petitioners contended that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and the deceased died due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

The police have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02AH4464.
SCCH10 28.

While discussing in issue No.1 with respect to the accident and negligence, it is held that the accident was occurred on the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA 02AH4464.
29.

It is the contention of the insurance company that, this respondent is not the insurer of Tata ACE vehicle bearing Reg.KA02AH4464 as on the date and time of accident i.e. on 28.09.2021 at 3.10 p.m. and it has issued policy in respect of the offending vehicle in favour of Santosh.
S and the same was valid from 29.09.2021 at 14.48 hrs to 28.09.2022 at 23.59 hrs., as such the policy was not in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.2 examined its officer as RW1 and RW1 stated that the policy was not in force at the time of accident.
Further deposed that as per 108 ambulance records the call received timing was mentioned as 28.09.2021, 13:21:20 hours for two wheeler accident.

Further as per the initial medical records Madhu Super Speciality hospital the history of SCCH10 incident mentioned as, "H/o RTA near Kamakshipalya, Vigneshwarnagar @
around 2.00 p.m. on 28.09.2021"
and itself shows that the alleged incident was not taken place as per the claim petition and crime records.
The RW1 has produced the MLC extract, endorsement issued by the Government of India and copy of application under RTI as per Ex.R.2 to Ex.R.4.
According to the petitioners case and as per the police records, the accident was occurred around 3.10 p.m.
The petitioner has not produced MLC or police intimation or case records.

On the other hand, the respondent has produced MLC extract as per Ex.R.2, it discloses the entry of patient on 28.09.2021 at about 2.30 p.m. and MLC discloses as, "H/o RTA near Kamakshipalya, Vigneshwarnagar @ around 2.00 p.m.
on 28.09.2021"
Further the details furnished by the EMRI Green Health Service Karnataka with respect to the call records of ambulance wherein the deceased was shifted to the SCCH10 hospital is produced as per Ex.R.2.

The EX.R.2 discloses that the date of service  28.09.2021 at around 2.00 p.m. to 2.30 p.m.,
caller contact details with call recording, cause of injury to Subramanya C. V.

The details of call records and call timing mentioned as 28.09.2021 - 13:21:20 hours base location, Kamakshipalya.
30.

Based on this, the counsel for the respondent No.2 argued that, the accident was occurred around 1.00 p.m. to 1.20 p.m. and there was a call to the ambulance to shift the deceased Subramanya C.V to the hospital.
The call records discloses the phone call was made around 13:21:20 hours it is 1.21 p.m.
The respondent No.1 owner has taken policy on 28.09.2021 and premium was paid at about 2:47:48 p.m.
The policy and payment receipt are produced by the respondent No.2 as per Ex.R.1.
The payment details discloses in Ex.R.1 at about 2:47:48 p.m.

Therefore, he submits that Jayalakshmi.R vs Santhosh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157193067/
8 the policy was not existed at the time of accident.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable.
SCCH10 31.

I have perused the police records and medical records as well as ambulance call records,
according to the petitioners and police records the accident was occurred at about 3.10 p.m., but the public documents like MLC and ambulance call records as per Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.3 are discloses the accident was occurred about 1.20 p.m.

The call records information provided by the EMRI Green Health Service Karnataka it clearly discloses the accident time and caller details as 28.09.2021 at 13:21;20 hours and service was made on 28.09.2021 at around 2.00 p.m. to 2.30 p.m., for injured Subramanya.
C.V. Therefore, the accident was occurred around 1.00 to 1.30 p.m. and the injured was shifted to the hospital at about 2.30 p.m., and the same is reflected in Ex.R.2 i.e. MLC record.
Therefore, the policy was taken on 28.09.2021 at 2.47 p.m.
The insured respondent No.1 paid premium after accident.
Though, the counsel for the petitioners has suggested to the RW1 as policy premium was collected by cash on 28.09.2021 at 11.30 am., but SCCH10 the same has been denied by the witness.
In fact, the documentary evidence is discloses the premium was paid on 28.09.2021 at 2.47 p.m.
Therefore, it is clearly proved that the premium was paid after accident.
Therefore, the decision relied by the petitioners are not applicable to the facts of the case.
Therefore, the policy was not existing at the time of accident, because the premium was paid after the accident.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Thereby the respondent No.1 being owner is liable to pay the compensation amount of Rs.20,23,000/ to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.3 in the partly affirmative.
32. ISSUE NO.4:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners SCCH10 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,23,000/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The petition against respondent No.2 insurance company is hereby dismissed.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the above compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for 40% of the compensation amount,the petitioner No.2 is entitled for 30% and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for 30% of compensation amount.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner No.1 shall be kept the 20% of her share in FD, in her name in any nationalized/scheduled bank of her choice, for a period of 3 years and remaining amount with accrued interest shall SCCH10 be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
